data.narrative:
Eclipse Space is a seed-stage space and aerospace company founded by Derek Huerta (former SpaceX senior manager of satellite payload engineering) and Kyle Leveque (ex-Astro Digital/Aquila Space). The target sector contains 5 public comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, and Sierra Space.

Standard valuation methods prove inapplicable here. Peer-median analysis fails due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables: while 14 same-sector peers exist broadly, only 1 seed-stage company was identified, falling short of the minimum 3 datapoints required for robust triangulation. Public-comp anchoring is similarly blocked; the Space & Aerospace sector median trades at 25.3x revenue across the 6 public tickers, but Eclipse Space's revenue figure is not on file—a common constraint in private company valuation where early-stage founders rarely disclose financial metrics.

Without disclosed financial performance or a sufficient peer cohort at identical stage and scale, quantitative triangulation cannot be meaningfully applied. Any valuation range derived here would rest primarily on founder pedigree and market-category positioning rather than comparative financial multiples. Progression to subsequent seed rounds, customer traction, or revenue disclosure would enable application of public-comp anchoring or peer-median methods. Until then, valuation warrants qualitative assessment and direct founder dialogue regarding capital deployment and near-term milestones.
